notes.automation_access: POST /api/automation-access answers; revocation.state tells input_stopped from stopping.
notes.post_harvest: POST /api/harvest answers as {status, body}. Off is never refused by the global action lock.
notes.refusals: The shared 409 body of every route that needs an idle emulator ({status, body}).
notes.start_transfer: POST /api/control start while only the standalone collector runs; operation is trimmed here.
notes.status: GET /api/status.harvest, one sample per state or condition. server_time is the fixed test clock.
notes.stop_operation: A person's Stop and the runner kill, every sample from the real route. cancel: POST /api/operations/<id>/cancel (also /api/scan/stop and /api/calibrate/stop) answers {ok, operation, stop:{state, reason, holder, by_this_request}}. state: stopped (the verified family exited AND the device lease is free) | released (a person released an unverifiable worker; nothing was signalled) | stopping (signalled, a member has not exited) | unverified (the stop cannot be confirmed; the operation stays the owner) | ended (it ended on its own or another writer settled it) | active (accepted/running/applying: defensive, the routes cannot return it after a cancel). reason, for unverified: worker_not_verifiable_lease_free|_lease_held|_lease_unreadable (the worker's identity cannot be proven) and lease_held_after_stop|lease_unreadable_after_stop (the worker is gone or was stopped but something outside the verified family still holds the lease, or the lease cannot be read). holder: the device_owned lease owner body while the reason names a held lease; owner pid and script stay null (the lease is not a process row) and lease.holders lists the live processes its lock files name. unverified_lease_free, ended and ended_after_termination are real-route races driven deterministically between the route's steps (the lease holder lets go after the release check; another writer settles the operation first, or after this request terminated the worker). by_this_request is what THIS request did, always present: {paused: harvesting was turned off by this call (a replay of another request's pause is false), requested: the stop was recorded on the operation, signalled: the pids TerminateProcess was called on, family: how the verified family ended (stopped|stopping|unverified|gone|null), released: an unverifiable worker was released}. state ended with signalled non-empty means this request stopped the worker and another writer settled the operation in the same moment: it was stopped, not found already ended. A Harvest Off never releases, only a person's Stop does. conflicts: a Stop that is answered 409 {ok:false, code, error, operation}. Before anything was done the code is operation_changed (stale revision or an operation that already ended; operation is the current one) | operation_unknown | operation_required (no operation_id / expected_revision) | not_cancellable; nothing was changed. Once anything was done (harvesting paused, the stop recorded, a process signalled, a worker released) a conflict is stop_outcome_partial: {conflict, error, operation (current), stop (how it stands now, with by_this_request)}, never a plain refusal; the client reads the operation again before stopping again. These routes are never refused with action_lock. repeat: a second Stop (repeat.*.after_release is the operation as the next read-write path settles it plus operations.stop_state(), not a route reply). kill: POST /api/control action=kill with {pid, created} as the list drew them; processes is the /api/status.processes projection, created is null when the scan could not pin the row.
